Package fr.univtln.bruno.samples.java101.tp1.factory

Class PersonFactory

java.lang.Object
fr.univtln.bruno.samples.java101.tp1.factory.PersonFactory
public final class PersonFactory extends Object
Small pedagogical factory to create Person instances.

This class groups named factory methods that make intent explicit and avoid the telescoping-constructor problem when many variants or default values are required. The factory delegates to the Person constructor in this sample, but in production code it could encapsulate more complex creation logic (validation, configuration, caching, or dependency wiring).

Factory methods are static methods that return an instance of a class. They are an alternative to constructors and can have descriptive names that clarify the purpose of the created instance.

Common factory method names (see Effective Java, item about static factories):

  • valueOf — convert parameters into an instance that represents the same value.
  • of — a concise alternative to valueOf (used in several JDK APIs).
  • getInstance — return an instance described by the parameters (often used for singletons or cached instances).
  • newInstance — guarantee a new distinct instance on each call.
  • getType / newType — variants used when the factory is declared in a different class and returns a particular type.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static Person of(String firstName, String lastName, int age)
      Create a Person with the given names and age.

      This method validates its inputs and normalizes string values (calls String.strip()). It throws a NullPointerException when a name is null and IllegalArgumentException when the age is negative.

      Parameters:
      firstName - first name (must not be null)
      lastName - last name (must not be null)
      age - age, must be >= 0
      Returns:
      a new Person instance
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if firstName or lastName is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if age is negative
